summary: The machine replacing its own boot loader through /dev/grubcore: three boots of one GRUB disk through SeaBIOS, under tests/cases/machine/grub_scenario.c

cases.behavior: bootctl grub writes a core image into the tail of the gap that is not in use and then selects it, so that the next boot runs the core it installed: the disk's unmarked core installs core B, the boot after it runs B and installs core A into the other tail, and the boot after that runs A; /dev/grubcore refuses a second opener while the first holds it and takes one once the holder has exited

inputs.cores: core-a.img and core-b.img of the root, the pinned cores that print GRUBCORE=A and GRUBCORE=B
inputs.disk: the GRUB disk on an MBR with an unmarked core, a recovery partition of 8 MiB and grub-test's ext2 root of 48 MiB

execution.cleanup: libetude-case ends the machine and removes the disk's copy, which it keeps after a failure

steps.does: boot the disk through SeaBIOS and GRUB, log in as root at the console, install core B with bootctl grub, and end the boot with reboot -f
boot the disk, log in as root, install core A with bootctl grub, open /dev/grubcore twice in one subshell and once after it has exited, and power off
boot the disk until the login prompt and end it with QMP's quit

assertions.checks: the first boot, of the disk as made, prints no GRUBCORE marker, so every marker after it is of a core bootctl installed
the second boot prints exactly one GRUBCORE marker, and it is GRUBCORE=B, so the core installed in the first boot is the one that ran
the two installs name two different tails, in the tail at LBA N, so neither wrote the tail the machine was running from
a second open of /dev/grubcore, while a descriptor of the first is open in the same subshell, fails with a message that says busy
an open of /dev/grubcore after the subshell that held it has exited succeeds
the third boot reaches the login prompt and prints exactly one GRUBCORE marker, and it is GRUBCORE=A, so the swap goes both ways

progress.means: a step of the manifest has ended

native.reason: bootctl grub writes GRUB's core image into the gap of the booted disk, which on the Lenovo is the accepted system's boot loader, and the case boots the disk through the firmware three times
